title: Microsoft Purview Audit: what the unified audit log records, how long it keeps it and what it costs
summary: Hold: the Dataverse automation shown only reads settings, and the claim that Dataverse auditing needs no Audit licence is not established by the sources. The page also omits the licensing qualification for sending Dataverse activity to Purview and the one-unfiltered-job restriction on concurrent audit searches.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: The unified audit log records user and administrator operations across Microsoft services in a searchable store.
claims.quote: Your organization's unified audit log captures, records, and retains thousands of user and admin operations performed in dozens of Microsoft services and solutions.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: An audited user or administrator activity generates an audit record.
claims.quote: When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record and stores it in the audit log for your organization.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Purview Audit has Standard and Premium tiers.
claims.quote: The following table compares the key capabilities available in Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium). Audit (Premium) includes all Audit (Standard) functionality.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Audit Standard is enabled by default for organizations with the appropriate subscription, subject to the SMB and unmanaged-trial exceptions stated later.
claims.quote: Audit (Standard) is enabled by default for all organizations with the appropriate subscription.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Audit Standard retains current audit records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Audit Premium adds retention policies for retention up to one year.
claims.quote: Create customized audit log retention policies to retain audit records for longer periods, up to one year (and up to 10 years for users with the required add-on license).

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention up to 10 years requires an additional per-user retention add-on.
claims.quote: Retaining audit logs for 10 years requires an additional per-user add-on license.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Audit Premium adds intelligent insights.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) builds on the capabilities of Audit (Standard) by providing audit log retention policies, longer retention of audit records, high-value intelligent insights, and higher bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Audit Premium provides higher Office 365 Management Activity API bandwidth.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) includes higher bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API, which provides faster access to audit data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Copilot, Cowork and AI application interactions are logged automatically as part of Audit Standard, with non-Microsoft AI billing enablement qualified later.
claims.quote: The system automatically logs these activities as part of Audit (Standard). If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Copilot audit records identify the interacting user.
claims.quote: These audit records contain details about which user interacted with Copilot, when the interaction took place, and where it occurred.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Copilot audit records identify when the interaction occurred.
claims.quote: These audit records contain details about which user interacted with Copilot, when the interaction took place, and where it occurred.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records

claims.quote: AppHost ... This property helps identify the application that hosted the interaction between a user and Copilot.

claims.claim: Copilot audit records reference the resources accessed to generate a response.
claims.quote: Audit records also include references to files, sites, or other resources Copilot, Cowork, and AI applications accessed to generate responses to user prompts.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: AgentVersion is a Copilot audit property containing the agent's version.
claims.quote: AgentVersion | The version number or version ID of the agent involved.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and agent records
claims.claim: Administrator activities related to Copilot settings are audited.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse auditing is a different log
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing logs changes to customer records in a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Dataverse auditing logs changes that you make to customer records in an environment with a Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse auditing is a different log
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing also logs user access within the environment.
claims.quote: Dataverse auditing also logs user access through an app or through the SDK in an environment.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse; Cost and licensing; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Dataverse stores its audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing is configured separately at environment, table and column levels.
claims.quote: You can configure auditing at three levels: environment, table, and column. First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse auditing is a different log
claims.claim: User access logging and Read logs are sent to Purview for production environments, with no licensing qualification given.
claims.quote: The option to turn on activity logging is only visible when the minimum MicrosoftOffice licensing requirements are met. ... User access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'User access logging and Read logs can be sent to Purview for production environments only; the option to turn on activity logging is visible only when the minimum Microsoft Office licensing requirements are met.'

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Retention follows the user's licence
claims.claim: The user's licence affects how long an audit record is retained and searchable.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: If logging is off, the evidence does not exist.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview auditing turned off existing audit records evidence audit status changes. Opened audit-log-enable-disable and audit-search: they state searches return no results, not that no evidence exists; status changes themselves are audited.
claims.fix: Remove 'If logging is off, the evidence does not exist.' The following documented sentence about searches returning no results already states the supported consequence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for Business Basic, Business Standard and Business Premium licences and must be enabled manually.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses, including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Unmanaged tenants using enterprise licence free trials do not have auditing enabled by default and must enable it manually.
claims.quote: Additionally, unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Purview audit searches return no results when auditing is disabled.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog returns no results when auditing is disabled.
claims.quote: Running the Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Disabling auditing prevents Office 365 Management Activity API access to the organization's audit data.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Disabling auditing prevents Microsoft Sentinel access to the organization's audit data.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the Office 365 Management Activity API or Microsoft Sentinel to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Audit licensing requires an appropriate organization subscription and per-user licensing to log and retain records.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: One year retention
claims.claim: Retention beyond 180 days up to one year requires the generating user to have Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or an E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on licence.
claims.quote: the user who generates the audit log ... must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: 10-year retention
claims.claim: Ten-year retention needs the generating user to have the 10-year audit log retention add-on in addition to the underlying Premium licensing.
claims.quote: In addition to the required licensing for Audit (Premium) (described in the next section), a user must be assigned a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license to retain their audit records for 10 years.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications; What to check
claims.claim: Auditing non-Microsoft AI user interactions requires enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Audit logs for non-Microsoft AI applications use pay-as-you-go billing. ... You need to enable pay-as-you-go features to turn on these logs.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go audit meter is the number of audit records processed.
claims.quote: Audit solutions | Audit logs for user interactions with non-Microsoft generative AI applications | Number of audit records processed

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: Enabled non-Microsoft AI interaction audit logs are retained for 180 days.
claims.quote: You need to enable pay-as-you-go features to turn on these logs. When you enable them, the system retains these audit logs for 180 days.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Non-Microsoft AI applications
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go requires associating the tenant with an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The enablement flow requires you to associate your Microsoft Purview tenant to an Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The Copilot audit page includes Microsoft applications, including Security Copilot, Fabric Copilot and Copilot Studio custom applications, in Audit Standard rather than pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: All Microsoft applications, including Microsoft Copilots like Microsoft Security Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, and custom applications built using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry are included in Audit Standard.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The Get started page instead lists Fabric Copilot, Security Copilot and Copilot Studio in AI data requiring pay-as-you-go, a discrepancy the concept page reports.
claims.quote: To audit user interactions with non-Microsoft 365 AI data ... you must enable pay-as-you-go billing ... This data type includes Copilot in Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Security Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and any connected or cloud AI application.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: per-record rate
claims.claim: The Copilot audit page states the billing unit but no per-record price.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview audit non-Microsoft AI audit-copilot per record rate pricing. Opened and read audit-copilot in full and purview-billing-models; audit-copilot gives the number of audit records ingested, but no numeric per-record price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Dataverse auditing
claims.claim: Dataverse auditing does not require an Audit licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse auditing license Microsoft Purview Audit license required storage capacity; Dataverse auditing no additional license. Opened manage-dataverse-auditing, auditing/configure and activity-logs-overview; none states this blanket licence exemption.
claims.fix: Replace 'Dataverse auditing: log storage capacity, not an Audit licence.' with 'Dataverse auditing: audit logs consume Dataverse log storage capacity.'

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging can be off; What to check
claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies auditing, with True indicating enabled.
claims.quote: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled ... A value of True for the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property indicates that auditing is turned on.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: The ingestion property always reports False if Get-AdminAuditLogConfig is run in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Although the Get-AdminAuditLogConfig cmdlet is also available in Security & Compliance PowerShell, the UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled property is always False, even when audit log search is turned on.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention follows the user's licence
claims.claim: Non-E5 and guest users' audit records are retained for 180 days.
claims.quote: If you have non-E5 users or guest users in your organization, their corresponding audit records are retained for 180 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Retention follows the user's licence
claims.claim: A ten-year audit retention policy is not retroactive.
claims.quote: This policy isn't retroactive and can't retain audit logs that were generated before the 10-year audit log retention policy was created.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Non-user actors get a fixed year
claims.claim: Audit records from service principals, system events and application activities are retained for one year.
claims.quote: Audit records generated by non-user entities (such as service principal actions, system events, and application activities) are retained for a fixed period of one year.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Non-user actors get a fixed year
claims.claim: The retention period for non-user audit records is not configurable.
claims.quote: This retention period isn't configurable and custom audit log retention policies don't apply to these records.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Non-user actors get a fixed year
claims.claim: Custom audit retention policies do not apply to non-user audit records.
claims.quote: This retention period isn't configurable and custom audit log retention policies don't apply to these records.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Audit records from core services typically become available 60 to 90 minutes after an event.
claims.quote: For core services (such as Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams), audit record availability is typically 60 to 90 minutes after an event occurs.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Microsoft does not commit to a specific audit record availability time.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't guarantee a specific time after an event occurs for the corresponding audit record to be returned in the results of an audit log search.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Records are not instant
claims.claim: Broad searches in large tenants may take up to 48 hours.
claims.quote: In large tenants with a high number of users, broadly-scoped Search jobs may take up to 48 hours to complete.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: The audit search date range is limited to 180 days.
claims.quote: The maximum date range that you can specify is 180 days. An error is displayed if the selected date range is greater than 180 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Each administrator can run ten audit search jobs concurrently without an additional restriction on unfiltered jobs.
claims.quote: Each admin Audit account user can have up to 10 search jobs running at the same time, with a limit of one unfiltered search job.
claims.fix: Replace 'each admin can run 10 search jobs at once' with 'each admin can run up to 10 search jobs at once, with a limit of one unfiltered search job'.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Audit Standard search exports are capped at 50,000 rows.
claims.quote: Export supports results up to 50,000 rows for Audit (Standard) and up to 1,000,000 rows for Audit (Premium).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Search has ceilings
claims.claim: Audit Premium search exports are capped at 1,000,000 rows.
claims.quote: Export supports results up to 50,000 rows for Audit (Standard) and up to 1,000,000 rows for Audit (Premium).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Admin units; What to check
claims.claim: A restricted administrator can search and export only user-generated audit logs within assigned administrative units.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Admin units narrow what an admin sees
claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can access non-user and system audit logs.
claims.quote: An unrestricted admin has access to all audit logs, including logs generated by non-user and system accounts.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse retention is stamped at write time
